newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras receipts remain suspended - bols.
newsitem.headline: Telebras receipts remain suspended - bols.

text.p: Trade in Telebras subscription receipts on Thursday remained suspended for the second consecutive day on the Sao Paulo bourse in connection with a legal dispute, a stock exchange statement said.

The bourse suspended trade after Communications Minister Sergio Motta on Wednesday expressed hope that an appeals court would rule in favor of the government in its long-running dispute with holders of subscription receipts in state-owned Telebras.
Telebras receipts fell 12 percent on Motta's comments before trading was suspended on Wednesday.
The Sao Paulo bourse on Wednesday asked Telebras for a clarification of Motta's remarks.

The company in response on Thursday reiterated it was awaiting an appeal court ruling on whether holders of the firm's subscription receipts will be allowed to buy preferred shares from a planned stock isssue, the statement from the Sao Paulo exchange said.
Motta told reporters a court ruling upholding the suscription receipt holders' rights would cost the government 1.0 billion reais.

In October last year, a regional federal court judge ruled in favor of the subscription receipt holders, rejecting a government request in 1992 to block the issue on grounds the planned share issue was undervalued.
The communications minister on Wednesday said that, even if the justices rule in favor of the firm, the decision should be submitted to the company's shareholders.
"The final ruling can take one, two, three years, and it has to be submitted and approved by the shareholders. And we (the government) are the majority shareholders," he said.
